name: Wemɛgbe
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.
catalog_citation: Gbéto, Flavien (2004). Esquisse de la tonologie synchronique du wemɛgbe, dialecte gbe du sud-Bénin. Studies in African Linguistics 33(1): 65-90. doi:10.32473/sal.v33i1.107339 (open access, journals.flvc.org/sal/article/download/107339/102660)
catalog_locator: Abstract, p. 65; §6.1 'Hypothèse de deux tons de base: H et B', pp. 77-78; §7 Conclusion, p. 85
catalog_quote: In this paper I show that Wemɛgbe, a language spoken in southern Benin, has two underlying tones, H and L, and that the surface tones M, LH and HL are derived by phonological rules. A H tone is inserted after an initial prevocalic voiceless obstruent (occurring in non verbals), creating a HL contour tone, when the vowel of the syllable is L toned. The LH tone is derived through a right-spreading rule from a L' prefix tone, which is postulated for all verbs in their imperative forms and for all nouns. [p. 65] ... On est donc en droit de dire que le wemɛgbe oppose un ton H à un ton non H, symbolisé respectivement par H et B. Les autres tons, à savoir HB, M et BH, seront considérés comme des allotones de ces deux tons de base et il s'agit de dégager les règles tonales de leur réalisation. [p. 78] ... Cette étude nous a permis de voir que, comme dans les autres langues gbe, le wemɛgbe oppose deux tons sous-jacents symbolisés par B et H. Les autres tons sont des tons dérivés de ces deux tons de base. [p. 85]
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.translation: This study has allowed us to see that, as in the other Gbe languages, Wemɛgbe contrasts two underlying tones symbolised by L and H. The other tones are tones derived from these two basic tones.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (26 pp., SAL 33(1) pp. 65-90, Acrobat Paper Capture scanned layer) opened and re-extracted with extracted text. Abstract, p. 65 (p. 1): "In this paper I show that Wem£gbe, a language spoken in southern Benin, has two underlying tones, Hand L, and that the surface tones M, LH and HL are derived by phonological rules." — verbatim apart from scanned artefacts ("Hand L" = "H and L", "Wem£gbe" = Wemɛgbe). §7 Conclusion, p. 85 (p. 21): "Cette etude nous a permis de voir que, comme dans les autres langues gbe, Ie wemegbe oppose deux tons sous-jacents symbolises par B et H. Les autres tons sont des tons derives de ces deux tons de base." — verbatim apart from missing diacritics and "Ie" for "l…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The only accessible primary description is a tonology: Weme Gbe is a two-tone language (underlying H vs L; surface M, LH, HL derived, partly conditioned by the voicing of the root-initial consonant). The paper makes no statement of any kind about word stress or accent, so no stress placement can be read from it.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress; the tonal analysis notes exceptions for coronal /t/ numerals (§6.4).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tonology of nominal and verbal roots in citation form (verbs cited in the imperative, the Gbe citation form). Dialect of Agonlin-Lowé and Akpadanou (commune of Adjohoun, Ouémé).
new_statements.identity_note: Gbéto 2004 describes the wemɛgbe of the villages Agonlin-Lowé and Akpadanou, commune of Adjohoun (Ouémé, Benin); Glottolog weme1239 lists no dialects, so this is the language-level entry. Houndekan 1983 treats the Adjohoun (Ajowun) chef-lieu variety. Names: Weme Gbe, Wémé, Wéménugbé, wemɛgbe, Wemenu.

tone_statements.citation: Gbéto, Flavien (2004). Esquisse de la tonologie synchronique du wemɛgbe, dialecte gbe du sud-Bénin. Studies in African Linguistics 33(1): 65-90.
tone_statements.quote: On est donc en droit de dire que Ie wem£gbe oppose un ton H a un ton non H, symbolise respectivement par H et B. Les autres tons, a savoir HB, M et BH, seront consideres comme des allotones de ces deux tons de base ... Cette etude nous a permis de voir que, comme dans les autres langues gbe, Ie wemegbe oppose deux tons sous-jacents symbolises par B et H. Les autres tons sont des tons derives de ces deux tons de base. Ainsi, Ie ton M est une realisation du ton IBI en contact avec Ie ton H.
tone_statements.translation: We may therefore say that Wemɛgbe opposes an H tone to a non-H tone, symbolised H and B (L) respectively. The other tones, namely HB, M and BH, will be treated as allotones of these two basic tones ... This study has shown that, as in the other Gbe languages, Wemɛgbe opposes two underlying tones, B (L) and H. The other tones are derived from these two basic tones. Thus the M tone is a realisation of /B/ in contact with an H tone.
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Two underlying level tones H vs L (B); surface M, LH, HL derived (floating L prefix spreads through voiced C; voiceless obstruents insert H). 80+ forms; nothing on stress.

sources.note: Nothing about stress/accent anywhere (full scanned text searched for accent, stress, intensité, proéminence, accentu-, emphase; 'accent' occurs only for the grave/acute diacritics). States that Wemɛgbe has two underlying tones H and L (B), with M, LH and HL derived (abstract p. 65; §6.1 p. 77-78; conclusion p. 85). Consonant classes condition tone realization; the dialect described is that of Agonlin-Lowé and Akpadanou, commune of Adjohoun.
